subject: burbot fish
title: This Fish Only Spawns Under Ice, in a Writhing Ball in Late Winter

scenes.text: Under a frozen lake in February, a ball of fish is twisting in the dark.
They're burbot, the only cod that lives its whole life in fresh water.
Many fish wait for spring. Burbot pick the coldest, darkest stretch of the year.
In late winter, under the ice, they crowd together into a big writhing ball.
Then they release eggs and sperm all at once. One big female can make over a million eggs.
So that silent frozen lake isn't dead. Something under your feet is spawning.

description:
Burbot, the only freshwater member of the cod family in North America, spawn under the ice in late winter, roughly February to March.
They gather into a large writhing ball and broadcast eggs and milt into the water; a big female can produce more than a million tiny eggs.
Would you go ice fishing knowing this was happening below you?
first_comment: Burbot can live 20 years or more, and they don't spawn until about age six. What's the strangest fish you've ever caught or seen?
